newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold shaky after heavy sell-off.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold shaky after heavy sell-off.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
-----------------VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - April 16--------------

Gold was battered after Tuesday's sell-off and was now on target to thrust down towards the February low of $336.15. It may consolidate for a few days, however, before looking at the downside, traders and analysts said.
GOLD -
Prices early on Wednesday were holding above the previous day's low of $340 when funds pounded the market, but the outlook was not pretty, analysts said.
"From a technical point of view, the break below $345...signals a test of $336.15 basis bullion," broker GNI said in a commentary, referring to the year's weakest price hit on February 12.
The short-term moving averages were adding pressure from above and would inhibit any effort to bounce, analysts said.
But the 14-day RSI at 33 was approaching oversold levels and might indicate that the market needed a rest before probing lower.
"A day or two of consolidation is likely to stall out under $343.60-$343.70, and give way to a final probe lower," said analyst Peter Rehmer of Elliott Wave International.
At 0840 GMT spot gold was quoted at $341.25/341.75, down 55 cents from Tuesday's New York close.
SILVER -
The market did not suffer on Tuesday as much as gold, but analysts were divided on the future direction.
Analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said the Comex May silver contract was susceptable to more downside pressure.

"Silver has weakened and is looking increasingly vulnerable to further tests of $4.65 support (the recent low). This level is currently holding but should there be a confirmed breach, prices could extend lower to $4.50," he said in a commentary.
But Rehmer thought prices were ready to bounce.
"Silver put in the "ideal probe under 468.0" to complete the corrective setback from last week's high, and is now perfectly positioned to rebound strongly," he said.
Analysts pegged resistance at the recent high of $4.80.
At 0900 GMT spot silver was quoted at $4.72/4.74, unchanged from Tuesday's New York close.
PLATINUM -
The market was heading down to the lower end of its range at $360, which if broken could send prices down towards $350.
Resistance was pegged at $370, then $374, which also is close to the long-term downtrend.
At 0900 GMT spot platinum was quoted at $364.25/365.25, up 55 cents from from Tuesday's New York close. --Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
